news.headline: RTW Investments and Susquehanna disclose expanded stakes in uniQure
news.summary: RTW Investments and Roderick Wong reported beneficial ownership of about 3.94M shares (5.7%), while affiliated Susquehanna entities disclosed an aggregate 3.34M-share (4.8%) stake in Schedule 13G filings accepted by the SEC on August 14. The filings point to continued institutional accumulation heading into the September AMT-130 data readout and Q3 BLA filing.

news.headline: Wall Street stays bullish on uniQure as shares hold gains into September data readout
news.summary: Stifel reiterated its Buy rating on uniQure with a $71 price target, citing the cleared FDA pathway for AMT-130 and the upcoming four-year data as the next major catalyst. Sell-side targets have clustered in the mid-$60s to $70s range following the June FDA turnaround, even as the stock itself trades well below those targets in the high-$40s.

news.headline: uniQure Q2 2026 earnings call: management details confirmatory trial design and AdCom expectations
news.summary: On the Q2 earnings call, Chief Medical Officer Walid Abi-Saab said an FDA advisory committee for AMT-130 is likely ("we most likely will have one... we welcome it") even though no formal request has been made, and management outlined progress toward launching the randomized confirmatory study alongside the Q3 BLA filing. Executives reiterated cash runway into 2030 and continued build-out of commercial-readiness infrastructure.

news.headline: uniQure says an FDA advisory committee for AMT-130 is likely and 'welcomes' the scrutiny
news.summary: Chief Medical Officer Walid Abi-Saab said the company believes an FDA advisory committee meeting for the Huntington's gene therapy is probable and that uniQure is preparing for it, even though the FDA has not formally requested one. The comments came amid broader 'regulatory jitters' across biopharma over unpredictable FDA advisory-meeting practices.

news.headline: Wolfe Research upgrades uniQure to Outperform, sees 'clear path to approval' for AMT-130
news.summary: Wolfe Research raised its rating to Outperform with a $65 price target, arguing the market is underpricing AMT-130's approval odds at under 50% when Wolfe models roughly 70%, with peak U.S. sales potential of about $2 billion. The upgrade followed the FDA's June agreement to accept three-year data as the primary basis for an accelerated-approval BLA.

news.headline: uniQure reports Q2 2026 results, confirms Q3 BLA timeline and cash runway into 2030
news.summary: Revenue rose to $5.8M and cash/investments stood at $810.3M as of June 30 after the June $259M offering closed, funding operations into 2030; net loss widened to $81.1M as commercial-readiness spending increased. Management confirmed the AMT-130 BLA remains on track for Q3 2026, said four-year Phase I/II data are expected in September, and detailed FDA confirmatory-study requirements (randomized standard-of-care control, Total Functional Capacity at 36 months as primary endpoint).

catalysts.label: Four-year AMT-130 data readout
catalysts.detail: uniQure plans to present topline four-year safety and efficacy data covering all 24 patients from the first two dose cohorts (12 high-dose, 12 low-dose), plus additional three-year follow-up on three more high-dose patients, from a dataset cut on June 30, 2026. Analysts (e.g., Stifel, Wolfe) view this as the key near-term catalyst ahead of the BLA filing and any advisory committee; the company is in a self-imposed quiet period on Huntington's-specific updates until this release.

catalysts.label: AMT-130 US BLA submission
catalysts.detail: uniQure remains on track to submit the BLA for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease under the FDA accelerated-approval pathway in Q3 2026, based on the FDA's June agreement that three-year data can serve as primary evidence.

catalysts.label: UK MHRA marketing application (MAA)
catalysts.detail: Following a successful MHRA pre-submission meeting, uniQure plans a parallel UK Marketing Authorization Application for AMT-130 in Q3 2026 based on the same three-year data package, giving a second potential approval route.

catalysts.label: FDA advisory committee (AdCom) meeting
catalysts.detail: Management believes an FDA advisory committee review of AMT-130 is likely given it would be the first gene therapy for Huntington's disease, and says it is preparing for one, though the FDA has not formally confirmed a meeting or date.

catalysts.label: Confirmatory trial design finalized / initiation
catalysts.detail: The FDA wants a randomized, concurrent standard-of-care-controlled confirmatory study with Total Functional Capacity at 36 months as the primary endpoint, and has indicated the study should be well underway (potentially fully enrolled) around the time of any accelerated approval; uniQure intends to begin the trial without delay following the BLA submission.

catalysts.label: Potential accelerated approval decision / epilepsy & Fabry updates
catalysts.detail: If the BLA is accepted with priority review, an FDA decision on what could be the first Huntington's gene therapy may land as early as mid-2027; uniQure also plans further clinical updates for its AMT-260 epilepsy and Fabry disease programs in H1 2027.

pulse: QURE remains in a catalyst-rich, still-binary setup heading into September: the June 2026 FDA reversal (accepting three-year AMT-130 data for an accelerated-approval BLA) triggered a wave of sell-side upgrades that continued through July and August, with Wolfe (Outperform, $65 PT, ~70% approval odds) and Stifel (Buy, $71 PT) both turning more constructive, while institutional holders (RTW, Susquehanna) added to positions per August 14 13G filings. The July 29 Q2 print confirmed cash runway into 2030 (~$810M, boosted by the June $259M offering) and reiterated the Q3 BLA/UK MAA timeline; on the August 7 earnings call management again flagged an FDA advisory committee as likely, though still unconfirmed. As of August 19 the stock trades in the high-$40s (around $47, well below sell-side targets in the mid-$60s to $70s) with no material new company-specific news since the mid-August institutional filings, as the company sits in a self-imposed quiet period ahead of the next real test: the September four-year data readout, followed by the Q3 BLA filing -- any data softness or a contentious AdCom remains the key risk given elevated short interest and the run-up in analyst expectations since June.
